summary.note: A re-reading of five merged pull requests: #605, #611, #624, #625 and #631. Each squash commit on main was read diff by diff against github.com/tailscale/tailscale at v1.102.4, replacing the previous edition, which covered eight other pull requests. Where engine behaviour mattered, the engine was read at the rev Cargo.toml pins (eabd2cf2). Each finding was confirmed on both the Go and the Rust side. Where the merged commit or its rustdoc already discloses a divergence, the finding says so, and engine-side causes are named as such. Nothing is fixed here; each finding is left as tracked work.

auditedPrs.notes: Squash 8c97d86. Ports NotifyInitialStatus. The snapshot is sent once, it is the session's first frame and carries the owed session id, and the NotifyRateLimit refusal is correctly unreachable because no rate_limit field exists. Three divergences remain. The initial bits arrive as several frames where Go sends one initial Notify. A subscriber outside Running can get a peerless InitialStatus. tnet has no --initial-status flag.

Squash 54866a4. A dependency-only change: it moves the four engine pins from 9d847a6e to eabd2cf2 to take russh 0.63.2, and it claims no Go port. Its two adaptations either preserve behaviour or move toward Go. whois `user` was always None under the old engine and is now the profile's login name, falling back to the display name, which is what Go's whois prints. The new StatusNode fields `tailscale_ips` and `expired` are only filled in a test fixture. That they are not surfaced yet (Go's PeerStatus.TailscaleIPs and Expired) is an older status gap, not a divergence this PR introduced.

Squash f03d958. A wording-only change to the `tnet exit-node suggest` notice for a pick the AllowedSuggestedExitNodes policy withholds. Its new claim holds: the user-initiated path logs `suggested_id` at warn (compute_suggestion in src/ipn/diag.rs). Measured against Go's runExitNodeSuggest, two divergences remain. The notice asks the operator to edit policy for a state Go never reaches. The empty-case line is not Go's text.

Squash 2ede56f. Adds the per-device recompute task, which runs on every netmap and when AllowedSuggestedExitNodes changes. It also makes "" a value the bus can publish and clears the cell silently when identity changes. Those three match suggestExitNodeLocked, setNetMapLocked, sysPolicyChanged and resetForProfileChangeLocked. Recomputing on every netmap is a superset of Go's triggers, but it does not churn the suggestion, because the engine keeps Go's sticky prevSuggestion (ts_runtime exit_node_suggest.rs at eabd2cf2). One divergence remains: a withheld pick publishes "" where Go publishes the best permitted node.

Squash f95330a. send_if_modified makes the compare-and-store one step, and borrow_and_update makes the front-load's read-and-mark one step. Together they close the duplicate-push and swallowed-push races against Go's prevSuggestion guard. One divergence remains, and the PR documents it itself. Completion order is not serialised the way Go's b.mu serialises it, so a race can leave the cell on the older answer.

gate.detail: All four steps green on main at f95330a, run with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4 and TS_RS_EXPERIMENT=this_is_unstable_software on the 1.95.0 toolchain. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` were clean. `cargo test --all-targets` covered 42 test targets: 1283 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. `cargo build --release --bins` finished in 7m 41s. Three facts about the machine, none about the tree. First, the default toolchain is a nightly with no clippy component, so the gate ran on 1.95.0, the version CI's stable runner uses. Second, the first test run under the long per-session TMPDIR failed only tailnetd's cleanup_refuses_live_socket, with `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN` (darwin's 104-byte sun_path); it passed when rerun with a short TMPDIR. Third, one run read a half-written draft of this file and failed tests/parity_audit_ledger.rs. That test reads PARITY_AUDIT.json, so it was rerun against main's own copy, where all 6 tests passed, and then against this edition, where they also passed.

findings.title: A policy-withheld exit-node pick is published as "" instead of the best permitted node
findings.detail: Go passes the AllowedSuggestedExitNodes set into suggestExitNode. Both suggestExitNodeUsingDERP and suggestExitNodeUsingTrafficSteering skip non-allowed peers before ranking (`if allowList != nil && !allowList.Contains(peer.StableID()) { continue }`), so the bus carries the id of the best ALLOWED node. The merged code takes the engine's unfiltered pick. When the allow-list excludes it, the code publishes SuggestedExitNode "" (suggested_exit_node_id over a withheld_by_policy response). On a policy-managed fleet whose engine pick falls outside the list, watchers are told there is no suggestion, where Go would name the best permitted node. The engine's sticky prev_suggestion is also set to the excluded node, so later recomputes keep landing on it. The code acknowledges this as engine ask #44 (the engine has no allow-list input), so the fix is engine-side.

findings.title: exit-node suggest tells the operator to edit policy where Go would suggest a permitted node
findings.detail: Go's runExitNodeSuggest prints one of two things: `Suggested exit node: <name>` with the `tailscale set --exit-node=` hint, or `No exit node suggestion is available.`. The allow-list filters candidates before ranking, so Go never reaches a 'picked but withheld' state. The merged notice says the policy does not list the node this build picked, points the operator to the daemon log for `suggested_id`, and tells them to list that node in the policy. So the advice is to edit policy, widening the administrator's allow-list to work around an engine limitation, which nothing in Go's behaviour calls for. The notice is accurate about this build, but the behaviour it describes diverges from the port target. Same root cause as engine ask #44.

findings.title: The empty-suggestion message is not Go's text
findings.detail: When res.ID is empty, Go prints exactly `No exit node suggestion is available.`. For the same case, exit_node_suggest_empty_notice (the function this PR edits) prints `No exit node suggestion available (no eligible exit-node peer right now).`, so a script matching Go's output does not match. The wording predates this PR, but it lives in the function the PR changed, and that function's tests pin it.

findings.title: An initial-status watch splits Go's one initial Notify into several frames
findings.detail: Go's WatchNotificationsAs builds one initial Notify (`ini`) that carries SessionID and State, Prefs, NetMap, InitialStatus, SuggestedExitNode and Policy together, then registers the watcher. The merged path sends the status snapshot, with the requested engine state and netmap, as the first frame. Prefs, policy and the suggestion follow as separate frames (emit_status_front_loads), and the PR's own test asserts that prefs arrives on the next frame, without the session id. A client written to Go's contract, where the first Notify holds everything it asked for, sees a partial first frame.

findings.title: A peerless InitialStatus outside Running or on a slow netmap
findings.detail: Go builds the snapshot with StatusBuilder{WantPeers: true}. updateStatusLocked then calls populatePeerStatusLocked, which lists peers whenever a netmap exists, whatever the backend state. The merged snapshot reuses Backend::status(), which queries peers only in State::Running and returns none if the netmap query exceeds STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT. A watcher that subscribes in Starting, or while the netmap is slow, therefore gets a peerless InitialStatus that Go would have populated.

findings.title: tnet debug watch-ipn has no --initial-status flag
findings.detail: Go's `tailscale debug watch-ipn` registers `--initial-status` ("set NotifyInitialStatus: send current ipnstate.Status in first message") and ORs ipn.NotifyInitialStatus into the mask when it is set. The PR says watch-ipn leaves the bit off because Go's --initial does. That is true of --initial, but the PR adds no way to set the bit from the CLI: both watch call sites in src/bin/tnet.rs hard-code `initial_status: false`. The ported subscription cannot be exercised from tnet the way Go's debug command allows.

findings.title: Concurrent suggestion computations can leave the cell and watchers on the older answer
findings.detail: Go computes and publishes under b.mu, so lastSuggestedExitNode and the bus always end on the most recently computed suggestion. In the merged code the engine call runs off-lock and only the compare-and-store is atomic. Three callers compute a suggestion: the recompute task, `exit-node suggest` and a watch front-load. If two of their computations finish in reverse order, the older answer is stored and announced last, and it stays until the next netmap recompute. The front-load in emit_suggestion_front_load can then send its own id followed by that older cell value. The PR documents this ('Ordering is not Go's') and relies on the engine's sticky suggestion to make it rare, but it still diverges from Go's serialised guard.
